That's not sufficient. Suppose file C (e.g. /usr/local/etc/mime.types) is in both packages A and B. Install A - this will create C Install B - this might overwrite C, saving a copy, or it might retain A's copy. Uninstall B - this has to know that C is used by A and not touch it MacPorts has an expensive but interesting approach.

Re: postfix making too many queries to LDAP Mike Kenny: While others here might be able to speak to the query mechanism, my own suggestion is to stop doing remote queries to LDAP. Just because it's possible, doesn't mean you should. I take dumps of the Windows AD (only the required attributes) on a two-hourly basis (during the day), and use that to generate hashed map files for the actual address resolution on each of the Postfix servers. Your own dump interval should probably represent the KPIs you might have in relation to account/mail account creation. Other than speeding up the query time by looking at the local maps, you're not annoying your LDAP administrators by constantly thrashing it (and the internal network) with lookups, spurious or not. Of course, there are probably performance trade-offs if your hash (or whatever) maps get too large
